Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Michelangelo Buonarroti (author, Wikidata Q5592), died 1564; Tommaso Campanella (author, Wikidata Q191850), died 1639; John Addington Symonds (translator, Wikidata Q538549), died 1893. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Michelangelo Buonarroti, 1475-1564; Campanella, Tommaso, 1568-1639; Symonds, John Addington, 1840-1893 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The sonnets of Michael Angelo Buonarroti and Tommaso Campanella, London : Smith, Elder, & Co., 1878, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/sonnetsofmichael00mich_0. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 100%, 79%, 75% of their four-word runs in the scan's text.
